one_line_reason: Most of the shortlist is agronomy/soil-science literature on Medicago sativa as a crop plant; the only two human trials either use alfalfa SEED (not leaf) or combine leaf with sage in an apparently uncontrolled study.

selected.population: 30 menopausal women with hot flushes and night sweating
selected.intervention: combination phytotherapeutic extract of Salvia officinalis (sage) and Medicago sativa (alfalfa) leaves, oral, 3 months
selected.primary_outcome: frequency/severity of hot flushes and night sweating
selected.why_selected: the only shortlisted human study that actually uses alfalfa LEAF (matching this catalog ingredient's plant part), though combined with sage and apparently without a placebo control group described.

selected.intervention: Medicago sativa (alfalfa) SEED powder plus vitamin E, oral, vs. vitamin E alone, 12 weeks
selected.why_selected: the only other human RCT of Medicago sativa in the shortlist, with a stated dose, though it uses seed rather than leaf and tests it only as an add-on to vitamin E rather than against a true placebo.

blockers: The only trial using alfalfa leaf itself (9677811) combines it with sage (Salvia officinalis) in a fixed product, and the study design does not describe a placebo control, so leaf's own contribution cannot be isolated.

The other human RCT (38103848) uses alfalfa SEED powder, a different plant part with a different phytochemical profile than the catalog's Alfalfa Leaf products, and adds it to vitamin E rather than comparing to a true placebo.
No dose is stated for the leaf-containing product, so it cannot be mapped to a catalog label amount.

excluded_pmids.reason: Soil microbiology study using Medicago sativa as a crop plant (rhizosphere bacteria for land restoration); no human exposure.
Soil-remediation review; Medicago sativa mentioned only as a phytoremediation crop plant; no human exposure.
Meta-analysis of soil carbon sequestration under alfalfa as a forage/cover crop; no human exposure.
Agronomy review of forage cropping systems in salt-affected soils; Medicago sativa treated as a crop species; no human exposure.
Food-science study of aroma compounds in beef from cattle finished on alfalfa-containing feed; an animal-feed context, not a human alfalfa supplement.
Plant agronomy study of alfalfa stem elongation and fall dormancy; no human exposure.
